hardinessNote: Hardy in most of the UK, approximately −20 to −15°C (H6 as nurseries give it; no RHS page).
visual: Deep pink tubular flowers in a main flush in late spring, then on and off through summer into autumn · compact upright bushy habit · green leaves
water: Water regularly in its first summer; after that only in prolonged dry spells. Pots need watering through summer.
soilWarning: Bone-dry or boggy soil costs you flowers
prune: Prune lightly after the first flush, cutting flowered shoots back to strong buds; remove a few of the oldest stems at the base every few years.
resilience: Easy and robust; flowers best in sun. Pests: generally trouble-free; occasional aphids, capsid bug or scale.
uses: Shrub borders · large containers · cottage gardens · low informal hedging · bees on the flowers
cvs: 'Red Prince' – red flowers, its pollen parent · ALL SUMMER RED ('Slingco 1') – red, same repeat-flowering series · 'Bristol Ruby' – ruby red, one main flush
sources: US plant patent PP33977, Weigela 'JS4' (Gijsbertus Verhoef): deep pink flowers, upright medium habit, continuous bloom spring into fall; seedling of 'JS2' × 'Red Prince' (patents.google.com)
Havlis catalogue, Weigela 'Js4' BIG LOVE, ALL SUMMER series: 1–1.5 m × 1–1.5 m, May–October, USDA 5
Hayloft (H6, 1.5 m × 1 m), Windy Ridge Garden Centre (1.2–1.5 m), Promesse de Fleurs (to 80 cm)
uncertain: name: Oscar's label reads 'Weigela flor. Big Love'; the patent calls it Weigela 'JS4' without a species (a seedling of 'JS2' × 'Red Prince'); the label's florida is kept, the code from the patent.
name: a US nursery sells 'JS4' as Watermelon Kisses (Bloomin' Easy); same code, so [Inference] the same plant under another trade name.
hardiness: no RHS page; H6 from Hayloft and the species' RHS rating; Havlis gives USDA 5. [Unverified] for the cultivar.
size: no RHS figure; Havlis 1–1.5 m × 1–1.5 m, Hayloft 1.5 × 1 m, Promesse de Fleurs to 80 cm; 1–1.5 m × 1–1.5 m carried. [Unverified]
peak: May-Oct from Havlis and the patent's 'spring into fall'; nursery months, the RHS has none for this cultivar.
toxicity: no ASPCA or RHS listing found for Weigela; one non-veterinary source says the leaves, flowers and fruit are not poisonous. 'No known hazard' is the absence of a listing.
compliance: US plant patent PP33977; UK plant breeders' rights not found, so left blank. [Unverified]
ratings, aspect, sunMin, water and prune: judged from the deck's sibling Weigela cards ('Red Prince', ALL SUMMER RED), not sourced for this cultivar.

hardinessNote: Hardy in most of the UK, approximately −20 to −15°C (RHS 166446).
foliage: semi-evergreen; rounded lobed leaves, metallic silver with dark purple veining, purple beneath
visual: Metallic silver leaves netted with dark purple veins like iron scrollwork, flushed burgundy in spring · slender red stems of tiny pinkish-white flowers in summer
water: Keep the soil evenly damp but never waterlogged; water pots in dry spells.
soilWarning: No winter wet around the crown
prune: Cut off faded flower stems; tidy tatty leaves in early spring. Lift and replant woody crowns deeper every three or four years.
resilience: Cold hardy; leaves scorch in hot afternoon sun. Pests: vine weevil grubs eat the roots, especially in pots; occasional leaf spot.
uses: Shady borders · edging · containers · woodland planting · cut flowers · foliage contrast
cvs: 'Cinnabar Silver' – silver over purple, brick-red flowers · 'Palace Purple' – deep bronze-purple leaves · FOREVER PURPLE ('Tnheufp') – glossy purple, compact
pollination: not applicable; grown for ornamental foliage
sources: RHS 166446, Heuchera 'Silver Scrolls' PBR: H6, 0.1–0.5 m × 0.1–0.5 m, clumps to 45 cm wide, pinkish-white flowers on reddish stems to 60 cm in summer (search snippets)
US plant patent PP12066, Heuchera 'Silver Scrolls' (patents.google.com)
North Creek Nurseries and Fine Gardening: silver leaves with dark scrollwork veining, burgundy flush in spring, part to full shade, rich moist drained soil
ASPCA, Coral Bells (Heuchera sanguinea): non-toxic to dogs, cats and horses
uncertain: size: RHS gives only the band 0.1–0.5 m × 0.1–0.5 m (text: clumps to 45 cm wide, flower stems to 60 cm); Burford 50 × 50 cm; North Creek 30–45 × 20–30 cm. The RHS band is carried.
peak: Apr-Oct is the foliage season it is sold on; flowers in summer (RHS), late spring to early summer (US sources).
breeder: sources credit Charles Oliver (Primrose Path, Pennsylvania), not Terra Nova.
toxicity: the ASPCA listing is for Heuchera sanguinea; applied to the hybrid as the genus. No RHS flag seen.
compliance: PBR from the RHS name suffix; the grant number was not found.
clay: 'no' because it needs sharp drainage at the crown; a judgement.
ratings, aspect, sunNeed and sunMin: judged against the deck's sibling Heuchera cards, not sourced.
